standard.title: Analyse information and identify perspectives
standard.description: analyse information and data, and identify perspectives
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S04): Students compared sources for evidence of change and identified perspectives, including whose perspectives may be absent.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse information across sources and identify multiple perspectives including those of First Nations Australians and diverse groups.

nodes.label: Multi-source analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare information across multiple sources to identify evidence of continuity and change, and draw analytical inferences.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse at least two sources on the same topic and identify evidence of change or continuity that appears in both.
nodes.typical_width: Compare information to find First Nations Australian, Dutch and French place names; analyse interviews with different people about the same management issue; use visible thinking to examine paintings across time periods; compare written information from a historian with visual sources.
wider: Analyse a set of sources that present conflicting information about the same event and decide which is more reliable and why
Compare what paintings of First Nations Australian rock art depicting Macassan contact reveal alongside written historical accounts

response_modes.reason: Multi-source analysis requires a systematic comparison approach — use analysis matrices to structure the comparison before expecting free-form analysis.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Triangulating multiple source types (visual, oral, written, artefact) is the most sophisticated analysis skill at Year 4 — students who can do this become genuinely capable historical thinkers.
success_criteria: Analyses at least two sources on the same topic
Identifies evidence of change or continuity that appears in the sources

nodes.label: Multiple perspectives on the same event
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain different perspectives on a historical event or contemporary issue, including perspectives of diverse groups.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different perspectives on the same event and explain what shapes each perspective.
nodes.typical_width: Explore perspectives of convicts, soldiers, free settlers and First Nations Australians on the arrival of the First Fleet; explore contemporary perspectives on school issues or environmental issues.
wider: Compare how perspectives on the First Fleet have changed over time (how historians now tell the story differently from how it was told 50 years ago)
Explore how the perspectives of the same event differ between its portrayal in Australian national narrative vs First Nations Australian accounts

response_modes.reason: Multiple perspectives from diverse groups on the same historical event is the most important analytical skill at Year 4 — use the First Fleet as the central case.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian perspectives on colonisation directly challenge and enrich dominant historical narratives — this is the richest perspective analysis opportunity in the Year 4 curriculum.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two different perspectives on the same event
Explains what shapes each perspective (experience, position, cultural background)
